title: Adaptive KV fidelity thermostat: dynamic per-cohort precision scaling (FP8/INT8/INT4) for GPU memory pressure
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Continuous batching and large KV caches are pressing GPU memory limits on high-throughput endpoints. Static per-workload quantization (int8/int4) reduces memory but causes workload-dependent quality regressions. We propose a "fidelity thermostat": a runtime controller that dynamically adjusts KV cache precision per request cohort (by model, prompt shape, and customer tier) balancing a token-level error budget against current GPU memory pressure and SLOs.

Goals: 1) Reduce steady-state KV cache GPU memory footprint by >=20% for hot models without exceeding predefined quality budgets. 2) Maintain latency SLOs for tail percentiles under continuous batching. 3) Provide deterministic rollback and transparent metrics for customer-facing regressions.

Hypothesis: Most degradation from lower-precision KV occurs on a small fraction of tokens (rare attention contexts). By adapting precision per-cohort and using a graceful fallback (FP8->INT8->INT4) with per-cohort error counters, we can save memory while keeping end-user quality delta below our alert thresholds.

Experiment design:
- Offline sweep: run large-scale replay using production prefix sampling traces (1B tokens) across Llama- and Mistral-family models. Metrics: token-wise log-likelihood delta, failure rate on QA prompts (EM/ F1), sampling divergence (KL), and human-eval spot checks.
- Runtime pilot: implement fidelity thermostat controller with three modes: conservative (FP8 primary, INT8 fallback), balanced (INT8 primary, FP8 fallback), aggressive (INT4 allowed for low-impact cohorts). Start with conservative on 5% of traffic for 48h.
- Cohort identification: model_id + route + median_prefix_len + customer_tier + recent_error_rate.
- Control signals: GPU memory headroom (percent used), SLO headroom (latency tail), per-cohort quality delta estimate (sliding window).

Instrumentation and observability:
- Token-level error histograms and cohort timelines.
- Per-cohort cost and mem savings dashboard (console-2025.02) and per-model rollback triggers.
- Alerts: auto-disable cohort when >0.5% requests have quality delta > threshold over 1h.

Acceptance criteria:
- Memory reduction: >=20% median KV footprint for targeted models in pilot.
- Quality: delta in perplexity <1.5% and QA EM drop <1.0% for pilot cohorts.
- Latency: p99 increase <5ms compared to baseline.
- No customer-facing incidents in pilot window.

Risks and mitigations:
- Unexpected distribution shift causing persistent quality regressions => add per-cohort quick rollback and canary gating.
- Rare edge-case tokens causing catastrophic output => keep FP8 fallback and token-level anomaly detector.
- Interactions with continuous batching that amplify kv-miss patterns => add batch-aware sampling and preserve batch ordering guarantees.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (simulation): complete offline replays and finalize thresholds (1 week).
- Phase 1 (pilot): conservative thermostat on 5% traffic for 48h; manual review and rollback if any metric violates.
- Phase 2 (gradual ramp): 5%->25%->50% over 2 weeks with automated gates.
- Phase 3 (opt-in): expose policy selector in Console for Dedicated/private customers.

observations: Offline replays show median KV mem saving ~24% with FP8 primary and INT8 fallback on hot seq2seq models.
QA EM drop concentrated on <0.2% of prompts, often long-context retrieval cases.
Latency p99 unchanged in microbenchmarks; integration tests with batching show small p99 tail increase (~3ms).
